info.title: GarageStack API
info.description:
GarageStack's own API: everything the web app shows and does, for scripts, Home Assistant and
anything else you connect.

## Signing in

- **On this page**, *Test Request* sends the request as you, with the session of the browser
  you signed in with. It is the real thing: a command goes to the car, a delete deletes.
- **From a script**, make a read-only token under *Settings, API tokens* and send it as
  `Authorization: Bearer gs_...`. A token only reads (GET), and never the export, the logs
  or the tokens themselves: every endpoint it can call carries a *Read-only token* badge.
- **The Homepage widget** sends the `X-Widget-Key` header (WIDGET_API_KEY) instead.

## Answers

- Times are UTC, in ISO 8601. Distances are km, speeds km/h, temperatures °C, tyre pressures
  bar, energy kWh and power kW, whatever units the web app is set to show.
- A refusal is a problem details body (RFC 9457) with a `code`, such as `trip.changed`, that
  stays the same between releases; `detail` says it in English.
- Each address may make 120 requests a minute (RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL_PER_MINUTE), and some
  endpoints allow fewer. Past that the answer is 429.
- A command's outcome arrives later, over the SignalR hub at `/hubs/telemetry`, as the car
  answers it. The command endpoint only says it was sent.
- `GET /api/health` reports the database, the MQTT broker and the Worker, without signing in.

get.summary: Get trip history (saved trips, then the ones not saved yet, including the trip being driven); points=false leaves out the fixes, format=compact packs them into a polyline and two arrays

items.description:
A position on a trip's path. Source is null for a fix the car reported as it
drove, and otherwise says why the point is there: left out of the JSON when null, so the trips
saved before it existed read the same.

endLatitude.description: Where the trip ended, or null for a trip without fixes.

maxSpeedKmh.description: The highest speed any fix reported, or null when none carried a speed.

avgMovingSpeedKmh.description: The mean of the speeds reported while moving, or null when none was.

movingSpeedSamples.description:
How many fixes reported a speed while moving: the weight to give
double? TripDto.AvgMovingSpeedKmh when averaging over several trips.

items.description:
A trip as the Api serves it. Id is the saved trip's id, or null for a trip
the Worker has not saved yet, such as the one being driven. The summary figures are read off
Points, so a client that needs only those can ask for
TripSummaryDto instead and skip the fixes.

A trip without its fixes: what the statistics page needs from a whole period of trips, at a
fraction of the size.

A trip as TripDto serves it, with its fixes as three arrays instead of an object
            each: about half the size gzipped, for a map that shows up to 90 days of them. Opt-in
            (`?format=compact`), so a script reading the plain format is not affected.
            Fix i is at string CompactTripDto.Line's vertex i (an encoded polyline at
int PolylineCodec.DefaultPrecision decimals, about 10 cm) and reported
IReadOnlyList<double?> CompactTripDto.Speeds[i]. IReadOnlyList<long> CompactTripDto.IntervalsMs[i] is the milliseconds since the fix before
it, or since DateTime CompactTripDto.StartedAt for the first, so a fix's time is their running total.
IReadOnlyList<TripPointSource?>? CompactTripDto.Sources[i] is its TripPointSource? TripPoint.Source; the array is left out when every
point is a fix the car reported while driving, as almost every trip's are.

x-codeSamples.source:
- GarageStack:
    href: https://YOUR_GARAGESTACK_URL
    description: MG Vehicle Status
    widget:
      type: customapi
      url: https://YOUR_GARAGESTACK_URL/api/widget/YOUR_VIN/status
      headers:
        X-Widget-Key: "YOUR_WIDGET_API_KEY"
      mappings:
        - field: evSocPercent
          label: Battery
          format: percent
        - field: isCharging
          label: Charging
          format: text
        - field: exteriorTemperature
          label: Ext. Temp
          format: float
          suffix: "°C"
        - field: isLocked
          label: Locked
          format: text

ApiReferenceStatus.description: Whether this deployment serves the API reference page, for the link under the token settings.

ChargeSession.description:
One charge, rebuilt from the telemetry rows around it. The battery kWh figures are the gateway's
drivetrain/soc_kwh as reported: MG's nominal 72.5 kWh pack scaled by the state of charge on
anything but a BEV series the gateway knows, so the browser decides whether to show them.
The power curve is fetched separately (ChargeSessionPowerPoint), only for the
session someone opens.

stack.description: Its stack trace, when the browser gave one.

page.description: The app's path when it happened, such as /map.

source.description: Where it came from: a script URL with line and column, or the Vue component.

ClimateScheduleMode.description: The climate mode a schedule starts. Each name is the value the gateway takes for it.

ClimateScheduleRequest.description:
A schedule's settings. StartTime is the time of day as HH:mm in TimeZoneId (an IANA time zone,
such as Europe/Amsterdam); Days are ISO weekday numbers (Monday 1 to Sunday 7), and none runs
the schedule once.

CommutePlaceChange.description: The place as saved (null once removed), and how many trips the change marked and unmarked as commutes.

CommutePlaceRequest.description: `Notify`: whether reaching or leaving the place sends a notification; left out, it stays as it was.

CreatedApiTokenDto.description: A token just made: Token is shown this once and never again.

DailyStat.description:
One local day for the statistics page: the averages of what the car reported that day, and the
day's total off its energy counter. A value is null when the car reported none of it that day.
`CounterTotal` is in the counter's own unit: kWh out of the traction battery on a plug-in
car, hundredths of a litre of fuel on a plain hybrid (see the frontend's utils/energy).
`SinceChargeTotal` is the same day read off the since-last-charge counter instead, and
`CounterUnbacked` says the day counter rose more than that counter allows, which is how
a car whose day counter cannot be trusted shows itself (issue #551). The frontend decides
which of the two to show, because only it knows whether the car plugs in.
`DistanceKm` is the day's total off the car's distance-of-the-day counter, read the same
way as `CounterTotal`, so the two pair up into an efficiency for the same stretch of driving.

DawarichStatusResponse.description: Deployment configuration and a credential check, never the URL or key.

LinkedPhoneTracker.description: Linked tracker identifiers only. No credentials or phone positions.

id.description: Where the entry starts: unique, and the same on every read, so the log viewer keys its list on it.

LogEntry.description: One log entry: when, how bad, which service, what it said, and an exception's lines if any.

LogPageDto.description:
A page of entries, newest first. Older goes back as `before` for the page after it, null
once nothing older is left; Newer goes back as `after` for what is written since. Reset
says the entries replace the list rather than extend it: a first page, or a live read that
found more than a page.

LogSourceDto.description: A log source and whether the API can read its files.

points.description:
The trip's fixes in the order they were recorded, at most
int MapMatchDefaults.MaxPointsPerRequest of them. A client with a denser trip thins
it first: the snapped line gains nothing from fixes closer together than the screen can show.

available.description: False when matching is switched off for this deployment, so a client can stop asking.

matched.description: True when Shape holds a snapped line to draw instead of the raw fixes.

pending.description: True when the matcher could not be reached just now and a later request may succeed.

shape.description: The snapped line as an encoded polyline (six decimals).

pointIndexes.description: One vertex index into Shape per fix that was sent, in order.

matchedKm.description: Length of the snapped line, which beats the straight-line distance through the fixes.

speedLimits.description:
The limits along Shape as run-length pairs (segment count, km/h), where a
limit of 0 covers a stretch OSM has no `maxspeed` for. Empty when none of the roads the
trip ran over carry one.

MapMatchResult.description: A trip's snapped line, or the reason there is none.

PhoneBackfillRequestDto.description: The earliest date to consider for an explicit historical backfill.

PhoneTracker.description: A tracker observed in Dawarich, without any of its positions.

PhoneTrackersResponse.description: Linked tracker identifiers and available trackers, with an explicit discovery error when unavailable.

PlaceAddress.description:
A place as reverse geocoding knows it: the parts a caller may want to compose into a label,
never a pre-formatted string, so the frontend decides how an address reads per locale.
`City` is the most specific settlement name (city, town, village or hamlet) and
`DisplayName` the upstream's own full label, a fallback for when the parts are thin.

PlaceDto.description:
A resolved place. All-null fields mean upstream knows no place at that coordinate, which is
different from the null entry a ReverseGeocodeResult carries for one it has not
managed to look up yet.

items.description: The POIs within the requested bounds that are already cached.

hasMore.description: Uncached tiles remain in this viewport, so asking again brings more.

available.description:
False only when the deployment does not serve this layer at all, which tells the client to
stop offering it rather than to ask again.

PowerTailgateSetting.description: Whether the vehicle has a power tailgate. See bool Vehicle.HasPowerTailgate.

code.description: Why, as a code that stays the same between releases, such as trip.changed. detail says it in English.

RdwInfoDto.description:
What the RDW said. bool RdwInfoDto.Found false means it knows no vehicle by the plate.
DateTime? RdwInfoDto.FetchedAt is the last answer, string? RdwInfoDto.LastError why the attempt after it failed.

RdwRecallDto.description: A recall, open or repaired; the texts are the RDW's, in Dutch.

RdwStatusDto.description: The plate (null when none is set) and the lookup for it (null until there is one).

points.description: Coordinates to resolve, at most int GeocodeDefaults.MaxPointsPerRequest of them.

precision.description: "city" for a settlement name (trip list), "address" for street level (parked car).

language.description: Language for the place names; anything unsupported falls back to English.

results.description: One entry per requested point, in the same order; null where unresolved.

available.description: False when geocoding is switched off for this deployment, so a client can stop asking.

hasMore.description: True while some points are still unresolved and a later request may fill them in.

SavePhoneTrackersRequest.description: The full set of trackers linked to one vehicle.

endLatitude.description: Where the trip ended, or null for a trip without fixes.

maxSpeedKmh.description: The highest speed any fix reported, or null when none carried a speed.

avgMovingSpeedKmh.description: The mean of the speeds reported while moving, or null when none was.

movingSpeedSamples.description:
How many fixes reported a speed while moving: the weight to give
double? TripDto.AvgMovingSpeedKmh when averaging over several trips.

TripDto.description:
A trip as the Api serves it. Id is the saved trip's id, or null for a trip
the Worker has not saved yet, such as the one being driven. The summary figures are read off
Points, so a client that needs only those can ask for
TripSummaryDto instead and skip the fixes.

points.description: The trip's points as they are now.

originalPoints.description: The points as recorded, when the trip was edited; null otherwise.

editedAt.description: When the route was last edited, or null when it is as recorded.

oneOf.description: Where the car stood before the trip, or null when nothing says.
Where the car stood after it, or null when nothing says.

suggestion.description:
Whether PreviousStop is far enough from the start, and near enough, that the
trip probably left from there: a trip saved before trips were anchored, which one tap can fix.

notBefore.description: The end of the trip before it: no point may be earlier.

notAfter.description: The start of the trip after it, or the recording line: no point may be later.

maxPoints.description: The most points a save may send.

TripEditor.description: What the trip editor needs to edit a saved trip's route.

TripLogEntry.description:
One line of the trip log: a saved trip without its fixes, plus what the driver recorded about
it. A place is null until it has been looked up.

TripPlaces.description: The places now known for one trip. Either may still be null when it is not resolved yet.

trips.description: The places now known for each requested trip; a place still null is not resolved yet.

available.description: False when geocoding is switched off for this deployment, so a client can stop asking.

hasMore.description: True while some ends are still unresolved and a later request may fill them in.

TripPoint.description:
A position on a trip's path. Source is null for a fix the car reported as it
drove, and otherwise says why the point is there: left out of the JSON when null, so the trips
saved before it existed read the same.

TripPointInput.description:
A point as the trip editor sends it: where, and when. The server decides its speed and
TripPointSource? TripPoint.Source, so a client cannot pass a point it placed off as one the car
reported. Every field is nullable so a missing one is a validation error, not a binding failure.

TripStop.description:
Where the car stood before or after a trip: a parked fix, or the neighbouring trip's end.
SuggestedAt is the time to give a point placed there: when the car left it,
or when it got there.

TyreChanges.description:
Each tyre's change against the other three, in bar: negative when it lost air the others kept.
Days is how many days with all four readings it rests on.

TyreHistoryDto.description:
A month of daily statistics (the same rows as /stats/daily, for the same chart) and, when there
are readings enough, each tyre's change against the others over TrendDays,
with the positions losing air (frontLeft, rearRight, ...) by the slow-puncture alert's rule.

lowBar.description: Below this a tyre is low: a warning on the dashboard and a notification.

goodBar.description: Up to this a tyre is fine; between it and HighBar it is on the high side.

highBar.description: Above this a tyre is overinflated: a warning and a notification.

dropBar.description:
How far one tyre may fall behind the other three over int TyreTrend.WindowDays
days before that is a slow puncture. Zero switches the alert off.

UpdateInfo.description: What the footer shows: whether a newer release exists, and where to read about it.

VapidPublicKeyResponse.description: The server's VAPID public key, which a browser subscribes to push with.

configJson.description: JSON blob of capability flags from info/configuration/* MQTT messages.

parkedLatitude.description:
Where the car was when it last parked: the position it is expected to stay at while the
engine is off. Null when the car reported no position then.

lastMessageId.description:
SAIC's id for the newest MG app message the Worker has dealt with, pushed or deliberately
not. The gateway publishes its latest message again every time it starts, and this is how
that repeat is told apart from a new message.

tripsRecordedUntil.description:
How far the Worker has saved this vehicle's trips: every trip starting before this moment
is in the Trips table, and the fixes from here on have not been cut into saved trips yet.
Null until the Worker has run once.

telemetryCompactedUntil.description:
How far the Worker has compacted this vehicle's telemetry into quarter-hour rows: every row
before this moment is compacted. Null until the first compaction.

licensePlate.description:
The Dutch registration, as string? LicensePlate.Normalize(string? plate) writes it, for the
RDW lookup. Neither the gateway nor SAIC reports it, so the user enters it. Kept on the
vehicle rather than in the browser's settings because the Worker looks it up.

hasPowerTailgate.description:
Whether the car has a power tailgate, so the boot can be opened and closed remotely rather
than only unlatched. Nothing in the vehicle data tells, and the gateway sends the command to
any car (one without a power tailgate refuses it), so the user switches it on.

VehicleCommandSent.description: A command as it was published: the gateway topic it went out on, and its value.

VehicleListItemDto.description:
A vehicle as the list endpoint returns it. `VehicleType` is the drivetrain detected from
the vehicle's reported hardware version (hev, phev, bev, or unknown while nothing has reported
one), served here so every client reads the same answer instead of parsing it themselves.
`HvBatteryCapacityKwh` rides along for the same reason: it decides how a client turns a
state of charge into kWh, and is null when the deployment has not configured one.
`SupportsTargetSoc` says whether the car takes a charge target, by the gateway's own test.
`HasPowerTailgate` is what the user set: whether the boot can be opened and closed.

session.description: The session cookie signing in sets. The browser sends it by itself, so this page needs nothing filled in.
session.name: garagestack-auth

apiToken.description: A read-only API token from Settings, API tokens. It only reads, and not the export, the logs or the tokens.

widgetKey.description: WIDGET_API_KEY, for the Homepage widget only.
widgetKey.name: X-Widget-Key
